title: Memory pollution: archived-but-cited (stale) and near-duplicate memories that surfaced in retrieval
description: M11b-quality pollution fixture. Observations are 60 days old (base_time 60 days before now) and the dataset opts into the M14 consolidation pass with decay.archiveThreshold raised to 0.2 — high enough to archive the low-prominence 60-day-old version fact (episodic half-life 30d), far below every explicit statement's prominence. The point-in-time probe then still serves that archived memory (as-of queries include archived rows) and REINFORCES it, producing the honest stale state the pollution audit detects: status 'archived' but cited within the last 30 days. The two procedural statements differ only in capitalization, so ingest's content-hash dedupe keeps both while their deterministic vectors are cosine-identical — the near-duplicate pair the offline merge pass (vector-gated, no embedder) leaves behind, and the third statement is the negative control (same type and project, dissimilar wording, must NOT flag).
